questions.q: The unwritten, unintended lessons about values and behaviour that students learn from school culture and practices are called the
questions.e: The hidden curriculum is learnt informally through school routines, relationships and rules, outside the formal syllabus.

questions.q: Gandhi's Nai Talim (Basic Education) is centred on
o: a useful craft or productive work
questions.e: Nai Talim, announced at Wardha in 1937, builds learning around a productive craft and links knowledge with work.

questions.q: The principle of 'learning by doing' in education is most closely associated with
questions.e: Dewey, a pragmatist, held that children learn best through experience and activity, and he saw the school as a miniature society.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Curriculum is broader than syllabus.
II. A syllabus includes all planned and unplanned experiences of a learner in school.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: A syllabus is the topic-wise outline for a course. The curriculum is wider and covers all learning experiences the school provides.

questions.q: In Eisner's terms, the 'null curriculum' refers to
o: topics and skills the school does not teach
questions.e: Eisner described the null curriculum as what schools leave out, which teaches learners that those things are unimportant.

questions.q: In Tyler's rationale for curriculum development, the step that follows selecting learning experiences is
questions.e: Tyler's sequence is: objectives, selecting experiences, organising experiences, evaluation.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a guiding principle of NCF 2005?
o: Connecting knowledge to life outside the school
Shifting learning away from rote methods
Making examinations more rigid and board-centred
questions.e: NCF 2005 asks for examinations that are more flexible and integrated with classroom life, not more rigid.

questions.q: Which committee prepared the detailed scheme of Basic Education after the 1937 Wardha Education Conference?
questions.e: The Zakir Husain Committee drew up the Wardha Scheme in detail. The Kothari Commission (1964–66) and Sargent report (1944) belong to later periods.
